description:
FILED s488 (Fable, 2026-09-17) from the s473v merge-review probes (the #1804 match record).  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main 5eb87b01 and on the s473v tree; #1804 did not touch it.

perlvar: "If multiple distinct capture groups have the same name, then $+{NAME} will refer to the leftmost defined group in the match."  Probe (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL), scratchpad probes/p-dupnames.pl:

  "ab" =~ /(?<l>a)(?<l>b)/            perl $+{l}=a   PCL b     (@{$-{l}} = a b on both)
  "b"  =~ /(?<l>a)?(?<l>b)/           perl b         PCL b     (leftmost DEFINED: the first is undef)
  "ac" =~ /(?<l>a)(?<l>b)?(?<l>c)/    perl a         PCL c
  "xy" =~ /(?<l>x)|(?<l>y)/           perl x         PCL x
  "y"  =~ /(?<l>x)|(?<l>y)/           perl y         PCL y

So `%-` (all groups of the name, in order, undef for non-participants) is right and `%+` takes the wrong end of that list.  FIX SHAPE: wherever the record materialises `%+` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the #1804 symbol-macro materialiser; before #1804 the eager set-match-vars), the value for a name is the FIRST defined entry of the name's group list, not the last write -- one `find-if` over the same list `%-` builds, so the two stay one reading (rule 11).  Also check `$+{l}` inside a `(?{ })` / the `\g{l}` backreference use the same rule (perl's \k<l> refers to the leftmost defined group too -- probe it).  Guard: rows in Pl/t/named-capture-01.t (the s473v file), inverse-verified.  Bar: the sweep (cl/ change) + the re/ companion leg (re/pat_advanced.t has the dup-name rows; read which ones are blessed fails with a #-less cause).
subject: `%+` with DUPLICATE group names answers the LAST defined group; perl answers the LEFTMOST defined one (`"ab" =~ /(?<l>a)(?<l>b)/` -> $+{l} is `b`, perl `a`) -- silent wrong; `%-` is already right
